criteria: I kept motion through a missed stroke.
I distinguished pitched and muted strokes.
My wrist and forearm stayed comfortable.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: You can count eighths for four bars while moving through muted, ghost, and chord strokes.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Return to air and one muted bar before adding Em.
selfAssessment.proves: Manual control of continuous strumming motion.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Automatic rhythm accuracy, tone, or measured tempo pass.

lessons.title: Ghost Strums
lessons.objective: Play two bars of downbeat strokes and ghost upstrokes, then transfer the exact 16-slot motion to Em.

steps.title: Read 16 slots
steps.action: Count 1-and-2-and-3-and-4-and for two bars: strike each downbeat and ghost every upstroke.
steps.lookCheck: Targets are beats 0,.5,1,1.5 through 7.5; no extra strokes belong.
steps.listenCheck: Muted downbeats are audible; ghost upstrokes are quiet.

steps.title: Prepare the mute
steps.action: Lay fingers lightly across all strings and use shallow pick depth.
steps.lookCheck: The hand returns after every stroke without squeezing.
steps.listenCheck: Hear short clicks, never pitched chords or scrapes.

steps.title: Run Play
steps.action: After the four-beat count-in, choose Play at 60 BPM. Rhythm score checks event timing, not mute quality.
steps.lookCheck: Review 16 targets, score, and actual BPM; it cannot see ghost motion.
steps.listenCheck: If input is uncertain, use Practice; abstention is not a failure.

steps.title: Transfer to Em
steps.action: Hold Em and play four bars with ghost upstrokes, then listen for even gaps.
steps.lookCheck: Keep chord fingers placed and the same 16-slot map.
steps.listenCheck: Hear Em only on intentional downbeats.

mistakeRecovery.observation: A slot is missed after a ghost.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Keep moving in air, say the next syllable, and restart the two-bar loop slower.
Flatten fingers gently without pressing and test one string.

mistakeRecovery.observation: Score is low but motion felt right.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Check input and repeat; score is rhythm-event evidence only.

criteria: I moved on all 16 subdivisions.
I reviewed score and BPM separately from mute quality.
I transferred the pattern to Em without wrist tension.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: Complete a 16-slot Play run at 60 BPM or faster with an 80 rhythm score, then self-check mute and comfort.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Use Practice at 40 BPM and isolate one bar before another Play run.
selfAssessment.proves: Rhythm-event timing for the authored 16-slot drill.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Mute quality, ghost silence, chord tone, or hand technique.

lessons.title: Checkpoint: Twenty-Four Bars, Self-Checked
lessons.objective: Hold counted down-up motion through a 24-bar original map and document recovery after missed strokes.

steps.title: Map 24 bars
steps.action: Use four muted, eight Em, eight C, and four G bars; count every 1-and-2-and-3-and-4-and.
steps.lookCheck: Section changes occur only on bar lines.
steps.listenCheck: Listen for pulse under every chord.

steps.title: Choose tempo
steps.action: Start 60–90 BPM and record the tempo you actually sustain.
steps.lookCheck: This is a continuity self-check, not automatic tempo certification.
steps.listenCheck: A steady slower pulse is useful evidence.

steps.title: Play through
steps.action: Keep moving for 24 bars; after a miss, ghost the next stroke and re-enter on its downbeat.
steps.lookCheck: Mark a stopped section rather than hiding it.
steps.listenCheck: Listen for pulse survival after recovery.

steps.title: Review
steps.action: Write where motion stopped, what chord or tone issue appeared, and one section to repeat.
steps.lookCheck: No app score is attached to this claim.
steps.listenCheck: Separate continuity, tone, and comfort in review.

mistakeRecovery.recovery: Keep count, ghost once, and re-enter on the next downbeat.
Mute one bar with the hand moving, then add the destination chord.
Stop safely and build eight bars before adding sections.

practiceSegments.instruction: Add C and G with recovery.

criteria: I counted and completed or documented all sections.
I used a ghost recovery after a miss.
I checked continuity separately from tone and comfort.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: Complete the 24-bar written run at a comfortable tempo and document recovery.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Reduce to eight bars and mute through transitions.
selfAssessment.proves: Self-reported continuity through the 24-bar map.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: 90 BPM, exact timing, clean chords, or microphone evidence.

lessons.title: Same Shapes, New Key
lessons.objective: Use a capo to raise the sounding key while keeping written open-chord shapes unchanged.

steps.title: Compare open and capo
steps.action: Play G open, place capo behind fret 2, and play the same G shape.
steps.lookCheck: Capo raises sound; it does not replace fingers or rename the written shape.
steps.listenCheck: Hear the same interval pattern higher.

steps.title: Check pressure
steps.action: Test every open string with capo 2, then play an E-shape chord.
steps.lookCheck: Capo sits just behind fret 2 and clamps evenly.
steps.listenCheck: Listen for rattle, buzz, or pinched notes.

steps.title: Transpose a set
steps.action: Play original G | C | Em | D open, then repeat with capo 2 while saying written names.
steps.lookCheck: Fingerings and omitted strings stay the same.
steps.listenCheck: Hear a higher register with the same contour.

steps.title: Try capo 3
steps.action: Move to fret 3 for one pass, then remove it and recheck standard tuning.
steps.lookCheck: Count position from the nut; do not stretch to compensate.
steps.listenCheck: Describe direction of change without claiming exact frequency.

mistakeRecovery.recovery: Move it behind the fret and use only enough pressure to hold strings.
Keep written chord and capo number as separate labels.
Remove capo, let strings settle, and check all six strings.

criteria: I distinguish written shape from capo sound.
I placed capo behind the fret.
I removed capo and checked tuning.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: Play the same shape set with capo 2 and explain that the key moved.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Use one chord at capo 2 and compare open strings.
selfAssessment.proves: Manual understanding of capo placement and transposition.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Exact concert pitch, intonation, performance, or capo detection.

lessons.title: Three Keys, One Original Study
lessons.objective: Move original G–C–Em–D between open, capo 2, and capo 4 while keeping written shapes and four-count bars.

steps.title: Read the study
steps.action: Play G | C | Em | D once open and mark two difficult transitions.
steps.lookCheck: The study is original and uses one chord per four-count bar.
steps.listenCheck: Hear bass changes at bar lines.

steps.title: Set capo 2
steps.action: Place capo just behind fret 2, test open strings, and repeat the four-bar study.
steps.lookCheck: Fingerings and C/D omissions do not change.
steps.listenCheck: The study sounds higher with the same contour.

steps.title: Set capo 4
steps.action: Move capo to fret 4, check tuning, and repeat the same map.
steps.lookCheck: Speak the capo number; do not stretch fingers.
steps.listenCheck: Compare register and clarity, not exact frequency.

steps.title: Log three passes
steps.action: Remove capo, restore tuning, and record position, best transition, and one tone issue per pass.
steps.lookCheck: Keep written shape, capo, and sound notes separate.
steps.listenCheck: If unstable, isolate the chord before blaming the capo.

mistakeRecovery.recovery: Reseat behind the fret and retest open strings.
Play four shapes open once, then repeat the same map at each capo.

mistakeRecovery.observation: Final pass is out of tune.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Remove capo, tune, and repeat only the affected bar.

criteria: I kept shapes consistent in all passes.
I checked capo placement and tuning.
I logged register, transition, and tone separately.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: Complete open, capo 2, and capo 4 passes of the original study with a listening log.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Use open and capo 2 first, then add capo 4.
selfAssessment.proves: Self-guided capo transposition practice.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Exact key, pitch accuracy, tone, or song measurement.

lessons.title: Checkpoint: One Original Study, Three Capos
lessons.sourceTitle: Checkpoint: One Original Study, Three Capos
lessons.objective: Play original G–C–Em–D open, at capo 2, and at capo 4, then review shape consistency and tuning.

steps.title: Prepare passes
steps.action: Write OPEN, CAPO 2, CAPO 4 above three copies of G | C | Em | D.
steps.lookCheck: Written chord names remain unchanged.
steps.listenCheck: Hear open pass as the reference.

steps.title: Check setups
steps.action: Before each pass test capo position, two open strings, and each shape's bass.
steps.lookCheck: Pressure is even and omissions remain unchanged.
steps.listenCheck: Repair rattle or tuning before playing.

steps.title: Play four bars
steps.action: Make one pass at each position with a calm reset while moving the capo.
steps.lookCheck: No microphone measurement is attached.
steps.listenCheck: Listen for bar lengths and register rising.

steps.title: Review honestly
steps.action: Restore standard tuning and write clearest pass, weak transition, and next practice.
steps.lookCheck: Do not turn tone impression into pitch claim.
steps.listenCheck: Your ear judges buzz and balance.

mistakeRecovery.recovery: Use spoken 1–2–3–4 before each pass.
Correct it open, then repeat that bar at capo 4.
Retune after removal and keep notes separate.

criteria: I completed or documented all three passes.
I checked tuning before and after.
I recorded clearest pass and next target.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: Complete the three passes and a tuning/shape review; readiness is self-reported.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Use two positions with a rest before adding the third.
selfAssessment.proves: Manual three-position capo study.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Exact key, intonation, timing, or capo recognition.

lessons.title: Counting in Threes
lessons.objective: Feel 3/4 as 1-2-3 and 6/8 as 1-la-li 2-la-li through spoken counts and chord strokes.

steps.title: Walk 3/4
steps.action: At 60 BPM speak 1-2-3 with an accent on 1 and play Em downstrokes for four bars.
steps.lookCheck: Each bar has three quarter counts; no fourth stroke.
steps.listenCheck: Hear strong-weak-weak.

steps.title: Group 6/8
steps.action: Count 1-la-li 2-la-li and brush two muted groups of three.
steps.lookCheck: Six eighths form two large pulses, not six quarter beats.
steps.listenCheck: Accent first and fourth subdivisions.

steps.title: Compare Em
steps.action: Play four bars in 3/4, then four in 6/8 with the same chord.
steps.lookCheck: Write meter above each pass and keep strokes visible.
steps.listenCheck: Feel two sways in 6/8 versus three steps in 3/4.

steps.title: Speak before switching
steps.action: Alternate one spoken 3/4 bar and one 6/8 bar, then add muted strokes.
steps.lookCheck: The switch is a count exercise, not a speed test.
steps.listenCheck: Listen for accent reset on each new 1.

mistakeRecovery.recovery: Return to 1-la-li 2-la-li and tap only two large beats.
Say 1-2-3 and tap only 1 before adding notes.
Speak a full bar of each meter before playing.

criteria: I spoke four bars of 3/4 correctly.
I spoke four bars of 6/8 correctly.
I heard the accent change.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: You can count and play both groupings with accents in place; this is self-guided.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Tap large beats and speak each meter without guitar.
selfAssessment.proves: Spoken and manual meter grouping.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Exact tempo, alignment, or microphone meter evidence.

lessons.title: Lantern Tide: An Original 6/8 Study
lessons.objective: Play original Em–C–G–D in 6/8 with two bass pulses per bar and counted recovery.

steps.title: Read the map
steps.action: Lantern Tide is Em | C | G | D, one 6/8 bar each. Count 1-la-li 2-la-li and bass 1 and 2.
steps.lookCheck: The study is original with no borrowed lyrics or recording.
steps.listenCheck: Hear two large pulses within every bar.

steps.title: Add upper brush
steps.action: Hold each shape and brush lightly on the two large beats.
steps.lookCheck: C omits 6 and D omits 6/5; keep bass in permitted strings.
steps.listenCheck: Bass anchors the bar while brush stays softer.

steps.title: Join four bars
steps.action: Play the sequence twice at 50–60 BPM and change after the second pulse.
steps.lookCheck: Do not invent a fourth quarter beat.
steps.listenCheck: Hear next chord arrive on new 1.

steps.title: Recover
steps.action: If a change slips, keep counting, play muted pulses for a bar, and re-enter on next chord.
steps.lookCheck: Mark the recovery bar rather than restarting silently.
steps.listenCheck: A muted recovery preserves compound pulse.

mistakeRecovery.recovery: Accent two large beats, each split into three.
Count all six syllables before changing.
Use smaller bass stroke and softer brush.

criteria: I counted six subdivisions as two pulses.
I kept the sequence for two passes.
I recovered one missed change by counting.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: Play two original study passes with two pulses per 6/8 bar and note meter/tone observations.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Tap two large beats on one chord before adding the sequence.
selfAssessment.proves: Original 6/8 study and recovery.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Exact alignment, tone, mastery, or microphone scoring.

lessons.title: Checkpoint: Meter Switch, Self-Checked
lessons.objective: Play an original map of four bars 4/4, four 3/4, four 6/8, then four 4/4 with spoken counts.

steps.title: Write map
steps.action: Use Em in 4/4, C in 3/4, G in 6/8, and D in 4/4; mark every count above the bars.
steps.listenCheck: Hear bar length change at each chord.

steps.title: Speak and tap
steps.action: Tap accents for all 16 bars before touching the guitar.
steps.lookCheck: Use one tap per quarter in 4/4/3/4 and two large taps in 6/8.
steps.listenCheck: Listen for accent reset at each section.

steps.title: Play the map
steps.action: Use one stroke per spoken beat in 4/4/3/4 and two bass pulses in 6/8.
steps.lookCheck: This is self-observed; no beat scorer is attached.
steps.listenCheck: If a stroke misses, keep speaking and re-enter.

steps.title: Review switch
steps.action: Write clearest switch, wavering count, and whether chord or meter caused it.
steps.lookCheck: Keep meter notes separate from tone and fretting notes.
steps.listenCheck: Your voice and ear judge grouping.

mistakeRecovery.recovery: Stop and speak 1-la-li 2-la-li while tapping two beats.
Count final bar aloud before starting next 1.
Mute strings and play accents before adding shapes.

criteria: I spoke the grouping for every section.
I completed or documented the stopping point.
I separated meter and tone observations.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: Complete the 16-bar map and document the clearest and weakest switch.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Practice each four-bar section, then pair adjacent switches.
selfAssessment.proves: Manual meter grouping and recovery.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Exact timing, tone, chord mastery, or microphone evidence.

lessons.title: Five Notes That Always Work
lessons.objective: Map A minor pentatonic box one from frets 5–8 and locate its A roots.

steps.title: Map the position
steps.lookCheck: Index anchors fret 5; ring fret 7; little fret 8.
steps.listenCheck: Roots are 6/5, 4/7, and 1/5.

steps.title: Place one finger per fret
steps.action: Keep thumb relaxed behind neck and hand over frets 5–8.
steps.lookCheck: Do not shift when reaching fret 8.
steps.listenCheck: Listen for even volume across fingers.

steps.title: Walk strings
steps.action: Play the map upward one string at a time, using alternate picking.
steps.lookCheck: All notes stay in frets 5–8.
steps.listenCheck: Hear one connected color rather than six starts.

steps.title: Resolve to A
steps.action: Use only box notes for four slow beats over an A drone and end on a root.
steps.lookCheck: A root is a musical destination, not a score.
steps.listenCheck: Ending on A sounds settled.

mistakeRecovery.recovery: Say the map and reset index at fret 5.
Move thumb behind neck and shrink motion.
Stop on each A root and compare nearby notes.

criteria: I can state each string's fret pair.
I located three A roots.
I checked pressure and evenness by ear.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: You can show box one from frets 5–8, name its roots, and play it slowly.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Use strings 6 and 5 until their patterns are stable.
selfAssessment.proves: Visual and aural map of box one.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Scale speed, picking accuracy, improvisation, or microphone evidence.

lessons.title: Box One, Up and Down
lessons.objective: Play the authored 23-note A minor pentatonic route across six strings with alternate picking.

steps.title: Read exact route
steps.lookCheck: There are 23 targets; high string 1 fret 5 is the turn.
steps.listenCheck: Listen for every fret before crossing strings.

steps.title: Set picking
steps.action: Start down at string 6 fret 5 and alternate continuously through string changes.
steps.lookCheck: Write D U above the first cell and keep it through the turn.
steps.listenCheck: Hear equal attacks without a string-change accent.

steps.title: Loop groups
steps.action: Loop strings 6–4, then 3–1 at 40 BPM, and join them.
steps.lookCheck: Do not substitute a different position.
steps.listenCheck: Check high-string crossing for gaps.

steps.title: Run Play
steps.action: After count-in, choose Play at 60 BPM. Pitch slots are measured; pick direction and tone are self-checks.
steps.lookCheck: Review 23 matches, score, and BPM; scorer cannot see pick direction.
steps.listenCheck: Use Practice if signal is uncertain.

mistakeRecovery.recovery: Loop last note and first next-string note with written D-U.
Center hand at fret 5 and lower tempo.
Keep pitch evidence separate and repeat at same BPM.

criteria: I followed all 23 string/fret targets.
I started down and alternated.
I separated pitch, picking, and tone checks.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: Complete the 23-slot Play run at 60 BPM or faster with an 80 pitch score, then self-check technique.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Loop the failed string boundary in Practice at 40 BPM.
selfAssessment.proves: Pitch-in-slot evidence for box-one route and BPM.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Pick direction, tone, technique, or memorization.

lessons.title: Checkpoint: Box One, Self-Checked
lessons.objective: Make two authored box-one route passes and document pitch evidence separately from picking, tone, and comfort.

steps.title: Prepare passes
steps.action: Choose 40–80 BPM and keep the 23-note route visible for both passes.
steps.lookCheck: This does not claim memory or clean technique.
steps.listenCheck: Hear the turn-around before starting.

steps.title: Run pass one
steps.action: Play up and down, then note missed slot, crossing, or noise. Rest before pass two.
steps.lookCheck: If using Play, record pitch and BPM separately.
steps.listenCheck: Listen for buzz and uneven accents.

steps.title: Run pass two
steps.action: Repeat the route with the same starting downstroke; record a stop honestly if needed.
steps.lookCheck: Do not omit difficult notes silently.
steps.listenCheck: Compare attack consistency, not only speed.

steps.title: Review
steps.action: Write actual BPM, pitch result if used, and one next technical target.
steps.lookCheck: The app does not award a clean-pass claim.
steps.listenCheck: Use ear for tone and hand for comfort.

mistakeRecovery.recovery: Mark first divergence on the map and restart that pass.
Drop to 40 BPM and use smaller pick motion.
Keep pitch result and tone note separate.

criteria: I followed the route on both passes or documented stops.
I recorded BPM and pitch separately.
I checked picking, buzz, and comfort.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: Complete two truthful passes and separate pitch from technique observations.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Use one string group at 40 BPM, then join groups.
selfAssessment.proves: Self-reviewed pair of box-one passes.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Two clean passes, exact picking, tone, or memory.

lessons.title: Down-Up Is Not Optional
lessons.objective: Establish economical alternate picking on one string and keep down-up subdivisions even.

steps.title: Anchor motion
steps.action: Play string 1 fret 5 once per click at 50 BPM with a small wrist-led downstroke.
steps.lookCheck: Forearm stays quiet and pick depth is shallow.
steps.listenCheck: Hear one even note per click.

steps.title: Double subdivision
steps.action: Play two notes per click, down on click and up between, saying 1-and.
steps.lookCheck: Upstroke returns through the string with equal distance.
steps.listenCheck: Listen for equal volume.

steps.title: Cross a cell
steps.action: Play 5–7–8–7 while preserving D-U-D-U and restart down after the cell.
steps.lookCheck: Write directions above the group.
steps.listenCheck: Hear one even loop without resets.

steps.title: Compare strokes
steps.action: Play one slow all-down bar and one alternate bar at same tempo.
steps.lookCheck: This demonstrates economy, not a universal speed limit.
steps.listenCheck: Hear less hand travel in the alternate bar.

mistakeRecovery.recovery: Reduce pick depth and practice a two-note 1-and cell.
Lighten downstroke to match upstroke.
Loop last note and first next string at 40 BPM.

criteria: I can say 1-and while alternating.
I kept pick depth small.
I corrected a missed or accented stroke.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: You can play a four-note cell down-up at a controlled tempo and explain the motion.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Return to muted strings and one down-up pair.
selfAssessment.proves: Manual understanding of strict alternate picking.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Maximum speed, tone, endurance, or microphone evidence.

lessons.title: Metronome Ladder, Sixty to One Hundred
lessons.sourceTitle: Metronome Ladder, Sixty to One Hundred
lessons.objective: Practice the exact high-E 5–7–8–7 cell through a controlled tempo ladder with measured pitch slots.

steps.title: Set the cell
steps.action: Use string 1 frets 5–7–8–7 repeated four times, starting down-up-down-up.
steps.lookCheck: The authored drill is 16 notes at half-beat spacing.
steps.listenCheck: Hear four-note groups and return to fret 5.

steps.title: Climb steps
steps.action: Start 60 BPM and raise 5 BPM only after a relaxed pass; drop 10 when a note blurs.
steps.lookCheck: Record highest comfortable and breakdown BPM.
steps.listenCheck: Listen for click alignment without force.

steps.title: Run measured route
steps.action: Choose Play at selected BPM; pitch score checks written notes and slots.
steps.lookCheck: Review matches, score, and actual BPM; it cannot see pick direction.
steps.listenCheck: Use Practice when signal is uncertain.

steps.title: Consolidate
steps.action: Repeat best tempo three times with rest; stop if wrist tightens.
steps.lookCheck: 100 BPM is ladder endpoint, not guaranteed result.
steps.listenCheck: Listen for equal volume before climbing.

mistakeRecovery.recovery: Keep last passing BPM and reduce step to 2–3.
Reduce depth and relax thumb-index pinch.
Stop reference audio, check input, and retry.

criteria: I used the exact 16-note route.
I recorded actual and comfortable BPM.
I checked direction, pick depth, and comfort.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: Complete a 16-slot Play pass at 60 BPM or faster with an 80 pitch score, then choose sustainable tempo.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Stay at last sustainable BPM and loop four notes.
selfAssessment.proves: Pitch-in-slot evidence for the cell and BPM.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Pick direction, maximum speed, endurance, tone, or tension-free technique.

lessons.title: Checkpoint: Eighth-Note Cell, Self-Checked
lessons.objective: Run the authored cell at a sustainable tempo and review pitch evidence separately from alternate-picking mechanics.

steps.title: Choose honest tempo
steps.action: Set 60–100 BPM from ladder results and keep 16-note cell visible.
steps.lookCheck: 100 BPM is not an automatic technique claim.
steps.listenCheck: Hear grouping before starting.

steps.title: Make two passes
steps.action: Play two passes with rest; record score/BPM or exact stopping point.
steps.lookCheck: The route is fixed but outcome is self-reported.
steps.listenCheck: Listen for even volume and relaxed wrist.

steps.title: Check boundary
steps.action: Loop first note after each 5–7–8–7 cell while preserving written pick directions.
steps.lookCheck: Continuous run restarts only intentionally.
steps.listenCheck: Boundary should not add accent or gap.

steps.title: Record result
steps.action: Write sustainable BPM, pitch result if used, and one mechanic issue.
steps.lookCheck: Keep measured pitch and self-observed technique separate.
steps.listenCheck: Microphone cannot prove picking or relaxation.

mistakeRecovery.recovery: Use highest comfortable BPM as truthful record.
Rest, lower tempo, and loop one cell.
Review route and input, then use Practice.

criteria: I completed or documented two exact passes.
I separated pitch/BPM from mechanics.
I chose next tempo from actual playing.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: Complete two truthful passes and document tempo plus technique self-check.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Use four notes at 40–60 BPM, adding cells gradually.
selfAssessment.proves: Self-reviewed alternate-picking cell.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: 95% mechanics, 100 BPM mastery, tone, or microphone evidence.

lessons.title: Notes Without Picking
lessons.objective: Create hammer-on and pull-off pairs and compare the fretting-hand note volume by ear.

steps.title: Hammer on
steps.action: On string 1 fret 5 pick once, then hammer to fret 7 without another pick.
steps.lookCheck: Index stays ready at 5; ring drops a short distance.
steps.listenCheck: Second note should speak.

steps.title: Pull off
steps.action: Pick fret 7, then pull slightly toward floor to fret 5.
steps.lookCheck: Index remains fretting destination; do not lift straight up.
steps.listenCheck: Hear fresh note, not scrape or gap.

steps.title: Move strings
steps.action: Repeat 5–7 and 7–5 on strings 1, 2, and 3.
steps.lookCheck: Use same finger roles and mute unused strings.
steps.listenCheck: Compare volume across strings.

steps.title: Place in time
steps.action: At 50 BPM use one pick on beat 1 and let legato note occupy beat 2.
steps.lookCheck: Do not add an accidental second pick.
steps.listenCheck: Hear pair inside steady count.

mistakeRecovery.recovery: Drop finger closer to fret 7 with firm relaxed fingertip.
Pull toward floor and mute adjacent strings.
Practice without click and match volume by ear.

criteria: I made second note with one pick.
I used a directional pull-off.
I compared pair volume by ear.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: You can produce clear 5–7 and 7–5 pairs on strings 1–3 with one pick attack.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Use one pair on string 1 and shorten finger motion.
selfAssessment.proves: Manual understanding of legato mechanics.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Volume consistency, timing, speed, tone, or technique measurement.

lessons.title: Legato Pairs, Three Strings
lessons.objective: Play the exact 12-note 5–7–5–7 route on strings 1, 2, and 3 with one pick per pair.

steps.title: Read the route
steps.action: Play string 1: 5–7–5–7, string 2 same, string 3 same; pick only first note of each pair.
steps.lookCheck: There are 12 targets; string changes follow notes 4 and 8.
steps.listenCheck: Hear destination notes without second pick.

steps.title: Mute around pairs
steps.action: Use index 5, ring 7, and light picking-hand muting on unused strings.
steps.lookCheck: Keep index down through pull-off; do not lift both fingers.
steps.listenCheck: Hear clean contour with no open-string noise.

steps.title: Loop each string
steps.action: Practice each four-note group at 40 BPM, then connect groups without an extra pick.
steps.lookCheck: Do not change position.
steps.listenCheck: Compare final pull-off with next string's hammer.

steps.title: Run Play
steps.action: After count-in choose Play at 60 BPM; pitch slots are measured, legato quality self-checked.
steps.lookCheck: Review 12 matches and BPM; app cannot see pick count or volume.
steps.listenCheck: Use Practice if input uncertain.

mistakeRecovery.recovery: Keep index planted at fret 5.
Loop last pair and first next-string pair.
Keep pitch evidence and practice volume slowly.

criteria: I followed 12 targets in order.
I used one pick per pair.
I checked volume, scrape, and muting.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: Complete a 12-slot Play pass at 60 BPM or faster with an 80 pitch score, then self-check legato.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Loop affected group in Practice at 40 BPM and count pick attacks.
selfAssessment.proves: Pitch-in-slot evidence for route and BPM.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Legato execution, volume, pick count, tone, or technique.

lessons.title: Checkpoint: Legato Pairs, Self-Checked
lessons.objective: Complete two slow three-string legato passes, keeping pitch evidence separate from pick count, volume, and muting.

steps.title: Prepare route
steps.action: Review string 1/2/3 each 5–7–5–7; choose 40–80 BPM and mark one pick per pair.
steps.lookCheck: Keep 12 notes and two string boundaries visible.
steps.listenCheck: Hear contour before speed.

steps.title: Run pass one
steps.action: Play slowly and note whether each second note spoke without a pick; rest and choose a weak pair.
steps.lookCheck: If Play is used, record pitch/BPM only.
steps.listenCheck: Listen for volume drop or scrape.

steps.title: Run pass two
steps.action: Repeat route while focusing on weak pair and stopping safely if tense.
steps.lookCheck: Record a partial pass honestly.
steps.listenCheck: Compare second note to picked neighbor.

steps.title: Repair
steps.action: Do three slow repetitions of the weakest pair and write the next target.
steps.lookCheck: Separate pitch, pick count, volume, and comfort.
steps.listenCheck: Microphone cannot prove technique.

mistakeRecovery.recovery: Rest, lower tempo, and isolate one pair per string.
Mute, shorten pull direction, and repeat pair.
Keep results separate and practice volume.

criteria: I completed or documented two exact passes.
I checked one pick per pair and muting.
I recorded the pair to repair.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: Complete two truthful passes and separate pitch from legato quality.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Practice one pair per string at 40 BPM, then join.
selfAssessment.proves: Self-reviewed legato passes.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Even volume certification, timing, tone, or microphone technique.

lessons.title: Where the Edge of the Hand Goes
lessons.sourceTitle: Where the Edge of the Hand Goes
lessons.objective: Find bridge-side palm contact and distinguish a pitched muted note from a dead click.

steps.title: Find bridge contact
steps.action: Rest palm edge lightly just in front of bridge saddles and play open string 6.
steps.lookCheck: Move millimeters; do not mute over middle of string.
steps.listenCheck: Near bridge gives short low-E pitch.

steps.title: Compare pressure
steps.action: Play no mute, light mute, and heavy mute with same pick motion.
steps.lookCheck: Only palm pressure changes.
steps.listenCheck: Hear ring, muted pitch, and dead click.

steps.title: Add eighths
steps.action: At 60 BPM alternate muted open low E for two bars while counting.
steps.lookCheck: Use shallow pick and relaxed wrist.
steps.listenCheck: Hear eight short identifiable notes per bar.

steps.title: Move to E5
steps.action: Hold string 6 open/string 5 fret 2 and test same contact.
steps.lookCheck: Palm remains near bridge; no full major/minor shape.
steps.listenCheck: Hear tight two-string attack.

mistakeRecovery.recovery: Move palm closer to bridge or reduce pressure.
Move slightly forward and add only enough contact.
Shrink stroke, pause, and practice one bar.

criteria: I produced pitched muted note.
I found comfortable bridge contact.
I kept two bars relaxed.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: You can shorten low-E sustain while keeping pitch audible.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Return to one low-E note and adjust palm by millimeters.
selfAssessment.proves: Manual palm-mute contact and listening.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Mute consistency, timing, tone, or microphone technique.

lessons.title: Iron Road: An Original Palm-Muted Study
lessons.sourceTitle: Iron Road: An Original Palm-Muted Study
lessons.objective: Play original Iron Road as palm-muted E5 eighths with a low-E pickup and counted recovery.

steps.title: Read the riff
steps.action: Use one open low-E pickup beat followed by three bars of E5 muted eighths; study is original.
steps.lookCheck: E5 uses string 6 open and string 5 fret 2.
steps.listenCheck: Hear low-E pulse and short two-string hits.

steps.title: Set the mute
steps.action: Test one low-E bar, then add string 5 fret 2 for E5.
steps.lookCheck: Palm stays at bridge and finger stays near fret 2.
steps.listenCheck: Compare tight E5 with dead click.

steps.title: Join four bars
steps.action: At 60 BPM count four bars with continuous down-up motion and ghost recovery after a miss.
steps.lookCheck: Retain the written low-E/E5 map.
steps.listenCheck: Hear even engine of eighths.

steps.title: Review take
steps.action: After two passes note whether mute, omission, or recovery limited you; repeat one bar slowly.
steps.lookCheck: Record bar and issue, not mastery.
steps.listenCheck: Tone and palm contact are self-checks.

mistakeRecovery.recovery: Reset palm during silent bar and re-enter next downbeat.
Loop low-E into first E5 at 40 BPM.
Reduce palm pressure and test low E.

criteria: I followed original low-E/E5 map.
I kept motion through a miss.
I checked palm, pitch, and unwanted strings.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: Play two original study passes and document mute, recovery, and tone.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Loop pickup into one E5 hit at 40 BPM.
selfAssessment.proves: Self-guided original palm-muted study.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Commercial song, mute certification, tone, or microphone score.

lessons.title: Checkpoint: Twenty-Four Bars, Self-Checked
lessons.objective: Hold an original palm-muted eighth-note map for 24 bars and document continuity, balance, and recovery.

steps.title: Map sections
steps.action: Use eight bars low-E muted, eight E5, and eight alternating; count every eighth.
steps.lookCheck: Keep Iron Road cell visible.
steps.listenCheck: Hear mute character through sections.

steps.title: Choose pace
steps.action: Start 60–80 BPM and record actual sustainable tempo.
steps.lookCheck: This is self-guided, not automatic technique proof.
steps.listenCheck: Listen for steadiness before speed.

steps.title: Play and recover
steps.action: Run 24 bars; after miss ghost next subdivision and re-enter downbeat.
steps.lookCheck: Mark reset bar instead of restarting silently.
steps.listenCheck: Hear pulse and mute return.

steps.title: Review
steps.action: Separate continuity, palm position, pitch audibility, and wrist comfort; repeat weakest 8 bars.
steps.lookCheck: Do not turn mute issue into microphone score.
steps.listenCheck: Use ear and hand for quality.

mistakeRecovery.recovery: Reduce stroke and build eight bars before rejoining.
Isolate E5 and check picking path.
Practice one ghost recovery on muted strings.

criteria: I completed or documented three sections.
I used counted recovery.
I checked balance and comfort independently.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: Complete the 24-bar map at sustainable tempo and record continuity and mute observations.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Practice one eight-bar section at 40–60 BPM.
selfAssessment.proves: Self-reported continuity and palm-mute observations.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: 100 BPM, exact timing, tone, or microphone evidence.

lessons.title: Thumb Keeps Time
lessons.objective: Establish alternating bass on strings 5 and 4, then add treble answers without disturbing the pulse.

steps.title: Assign thumb
steps.action: Hold C; thumb plays string 5 on beat 1 and string 4 on beat 3.
steps.lookCheck: String 6 remains silent in C.
steps.listenCheck: Hear two low pulses.

steps.title: Count bass
steps.action: At 50 BPM play bass–rest–bass–rest for four bars, saying 1–2–3–4.
steps.lookCheck: Thumb returns close to next string.
steps.listenCheck: Hear stable frame.

steps.title: Add treble
steps.action: Use index string 3 and middle string 2 on beats 2 and 4.
steps.lookCheck: Treble fingers do not pull strings sideways.
steps.listenCheck: Hear bass on 1/3 and answers on 2/4.

steps.title: Change chord
steps.action: Play one bar C and one G while preserving thumb plan.
steps.lookCheck: G thumb can use strings 6 and 5; keep treble quiet.
steps.listenCheck: Listen for bass through change.

mistakeRecovery.recovery: Return to thumb-only bass and keep stroke close.
Remove I/M, restore beats 1/3, add one answer.
Mute string 6 and begin on string 5.

criteria: Thumb stayed on assigned bass strings.
I heard bass on 1 and 3.
I added treble without losing pulse.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: You can play four bars of alternating bass and add simple treble answers.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Remove treble and restore two bass pulses.
selfAssessment.proves: Manual understanding of fingerstyle roles.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Continuity, timing, tone, independence, or microphone evidence.

lessons.title: Alternating Bass
lessons.objective: Play 16 alternating open A/D bass targets, then add a quiet treble answer while preserving the measured route.

steps.title: Read bass route
steps.action: Targets alternate string 5 open A2 and string 4 open D3 for 16 quarter notes; thumb only first.
steps.lookCheck: Odd targets are string 5/A2; even are string 4/D3.
steps.listenCheck: Hear A–D walking pattern.

steps.title: Place thumb
steps.action: At 60 BPM play one bass per click and let each ring until next.
steps.lookCheck: Use small strokes; fingers rest without sounding.
steps.listenCheck: Hear even pulse and no treble.

steps.title: Add answer
steps.action: After thumb pass, add index on string 3 between bass notes; treble is unmeasured.
steps.lookCheck: Thumb still owns every target.
steps.listenCheck: Bass should stay louder and even.

steps.title: Run Play
steps.action: After count-in choose Play at 60 BPM; result checks 16 bass pitches and slots only.
steps.lookCheck: Review score and BPM; app cannot know thumb use or treble balance.
steps.listenCheck: Use Practice when input uncertain.

mistakeRecovery.recovery: Say A–D and loop the two-note pair starting string 5.
Remove treble and complete thumb-only pass.
Keep pitch evidence and practice four-bar continuity.

criteria: I followed all 16 A/D targets.
Thumb played each measured bass.
I checked treble, continuity, and strings.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: Complete a 16-slot Play pass at 60 BPM or faster with an 80 pitch score, then self-check fingerstyle.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Use Practice at 40 BPM for thumb-only pairs.
selfAssessment.proves: Pitch-in-slot evidence for bass route and BPM.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Thumb technique, groove, tone, or full fingerstyle coordination.

lessons.title: Checkpoint: Alternating Bass, Self-Checked
lessons.objective: Play an original 16-bar C–G fingerstyle map and document bass steadiness, continuity, and treble balance.

steps.title: Read map
steps.action: Use C four bars, G four, C four, G four; alternate bass and add string 3 answer on beats 2/4.
steps.lookCheck: C omits 6; G may use 6/5 basses.
steps.listenCheck: Hear two bass pulses and treble answers.

steps.title: Run thumb-only
steps.action: Play 16 bars at 50–60 BPM, changing on bar lines; note breaks.
steps.lookCheck: This is self-check, not microphone continuity measurement.
steps.listenCheck: Listen for bass through C↔G.

steps.title: Add treble
steps.action: Repeat with index answer, softer than bass; allow silent bar-line reset.
steps.lookCheck: Do not add treble to cover missed bass.
steps.listenCheck: Compare bass and treble balance.

steps.title: Repair
steps.action: Choose a four-bar section for three slow repetitions and write next target.
steps.lookCheck: Separate pitch result from fingerstyle qualities.
steps.listenCheck: App cannot infer thumb use or independence.

mistakeRecovery.recovery: Loop one C bar into G with bass only, then add treble.
Use lighter index and return to bass-only.
Stop safely and build four-bar blocks.

criteria: I completed or documented all four sections.
Thumb bass stayed steady through changes.
I wrote separate continuity and balance notes.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: Complete the map or document exact repair block with separate fingerstyle self-check.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Practice one bass-only four-bar block, then add treble.
selfAssessment.proves: Self-reviewed continuity and role balance.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Unbroken certification, timing, tone, thumb detection, or microphone evidence.
